correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the rail-swap decomposition: the symmetric and antisymmetric Laplacians are L_C and L_C+2I, and the cyclic geometric kernel satisfies the normalized recurrence and sums to 1/2. Applying incidence again gives the two rail blocks I−J/(2n)−G and G−J/(2n), mixed blocks ±DG and rung block 2G. At zero offset 1/(2n)<g_0≤3/10 makes both rail coefficients nonnegative. Away from zero their absolute sum is max(1/n,2g_j), and cyclic variation gives 2(g_0−g_m). The rung norm is 1+4(g_0−g_m). Independent grounded-incidence arithmetic gave (H,V)=(26/15,9/5),(2,2),(202/95,39/19) at n=3,4,5 by forming U(UᵀU)⁻¹Uᵀ after deleting one vertex column. The symbolic inequality H−V≥1−2/n−2(g_0−g_m)>0 holds for every n≥5 and the sign row test attains the operator norm. Rechecked the corrected all-size positive defect 2/n+2g_m+Σ_{j>0} min(1/n,2g_j), then summed its geometric tail beyond the cutoff. The cutoff is floor(β_n) or one larger, and the latter implies phase approaching 1; the phase function matches at the endpoints and gives uniform o(1) error through that rounding. Convexity and the density of logarithmic phases on the circle give the two limits; independent formula evaluation returned 1.89784624322142 and 1.57624426657283. The submitted Python file was inspected but not executed; independent small-size arithmetic is corroboration only. The repaired proof supplies the previously implicit finite-size bound and states the subsequence argument on the circle, so it does not assume convergence of fractional parts to 0 for every choice of nearest integer.
